results.title: Lium vs Lambda: same GPUs, lower prices, built for AI agents | lium.io
highlights:
# Lium vs Lambda: same GPUs, lower prices, built for AI agents

We compared on-demand H100, H200, B200 and A6000 prices, billing, storage and AI agent support across Lium and Lambda on 29 October 2026.

Lium team· 29 October 2026· 7 min read

Lium is the better place for developers and AI agents to rent GPUs. On 29 October 2026, Lium beat Lambda on every on-demand GPU we compared, saving $190.08 a day on an 8x H100 SXM node and cutting single H100 and A6000 prices by more than half. Lium also bills by the second instead of the minute and gives agents like Claude Code and Codex their own server-enforced spend caps.

Why Lium beats Lambda:

- Lower on-demand prices on every GPU we compared: $1.79 vs $4.29 on 1x H100 SXM, $3.00 vs $3.99 per GPU on 8x H100 SXM, $5.90 vs $6.99 on 1x B200, and $0.42 vs $1.09 on 1x RTX A6000.
- On-demand 8x H200 NVLink nodes at $3.50/GPU/hour: Lambda does not list the H200 in its on-demand instance table.
- Per-second billing with `--ttl` auto-removal: Lium bills to the second with no minimum or rounding, while Lambda bills by the minute.
- Built for AI agents: budgeted API keys enforced on Lium's servers, one-call account creation without an email address, a docs MCP server, `llms.txt`, and the `lium` CLI and Python SDK.
- Automatic failover and verified hardware: pods that never reach `RUNNING` are not charged, `--verify-gpus` checks `nvidia-smi` against your bill, and a validator tests every connected node every 15 minutes.
- Pay with card, stablecoins, or TAO: start your first pod with a balance covering 15 minutes of its price ($6.00 for the 8x H100 node).

## On-demand GPU prices on 29 October 2026

Lium's Secure tier cost less than Lambda's on-demand instances on every GPU in the table below, and Lium also offers on-demand 8x H200 NVLink nodes. All prices below were read on 29 October 2026 at 15:08 UTC. Lium is a marketplace where independent providers set their own prices, so these asks move during the day; Lambda's on-demand instance rates are charged plus applicable sales tax, VAT, or GST. Sources: Lium's public node feed and lambda.ai/pricing. Prices are per GPU per hour.

| GPU | Lium, Secure | Lambda |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM, 1 GPU | $1.79 | $4.29 (1x instance) |
| H100 SXM, 8-GPU NVLink node | $3.00 ($24.00/hr whole node) | $3.99 (8x instance) |
| B200, 1 GPU | $5.90 | $6.99 (1x instance) |
| RTX A6000 48 GB, 1 GPU | $0.42 | $1.09 (1x instance) |
| H200, 8-GPU NVLink node | $3.50 | not in Lambda's on-demand instance table |

A few details behind the table:

- Lium lists the H100 SXM as `H100 80GB HBM3`. The 8x H100 node is rented whole at $24.00 an hour for the machine.
- Lambda also lists an 8x B200 instance at $6.69 per GPU per hour.
- For larger multi-node jobs, Lambda's 1-Click Clusters (16+ H100s, booked for 2 weeks to 1 year) list $6.16 per GPU per hour for 16 GPUs, and reserved capacity is "contact us".

Because Lium providers set their own prices, check today's live asks before you rent on /pricing, the H100 page, the B200 page, or in your terminal with `lium ls`.

## Three rental cost examples

Lium costs less in each of these three rental examples. The totals compare equal rental durations and cover compute only, before storage, transfer, and tax:

- 24 hours on an 8x H100 SXM NVLink node:

- Lium: $3.00 × 8 × 24 = $576.00
- Lambda: $3.99 × 8 × 24 = $766.08
- Result: Lium saves $190.08 per day.
- 8 hours on a single B200:

- Lium: $5.90 × 8 = $47.20
- Lambda: $6.99 × 8 = $55.92
- Result: Lium saves $8.72.
- A week of RTX A6000 iteration (8 hours a day for 5 days = 40 GPU-hours):

- Lium: $0.42 × 40 = $16.80
- Lambda: $1.09 × 40 = $43.60

...

Lium bills pods per second at the listed price, with no minimum and no rounding. Lambda advertises "Pay by the minute". On Lium, you can also pass `lium up --ttl 24h` to schedule pod removal at rent time, so a forgotten job stops billing automatically.

To start your first pod on Lium, you only need a balance covering 15 minutes of its price: $6.00 for the $24.00/hour 8x H100 node. You can top up with a card, stablecoins, or TAO.

...

### How much cheaper is Lium than Lambda on an 8x H100 node?

On 29 October 2026 at 15:08 UTC, an 8x H100 SXM NVLink Secure node on Lium was $3.00 per GPU per hour ($24.00/hour for the whole machine) versus $3.99 per GPU per hour on Lambda. Over a 24-hour run, Lium costs $576.00 against Lambda's $766.08, saving $190.08 per day.

### Does Lium have H200 GPUs on demand?

Yes. On 29 October 2026, Lium had 8-GPU H200 NVLink Secure nodes at $3.50 per GPU per hour. Lambda did not list the H200 in its on-demand instance table.

results.title: Fine-tuning an open model on a rented GPU: what an hour costs in 2026
results.author: Partner
highlights:
# Fine-tuning an open model on a rented GPU: what an hour costs in 2026 

 Oct 21, 2026 

 by Partner 

Fine-tuning used to mean a cluster, a contract and a week of setup. In 2026 most teams adapt an open model such as Llama, Qwen or Mistral to their own data with LoRA, a method that trains a small set of extra weights instead of the whole model. A LoRA run on a mid-size model is a job measured in minutes to hours, not weeks, so the question has changed from "can we afford a GPU cluster?" to "what does one hour of the right GPU cost, and how fast can I get it?"

This piece answers that with live numbers from Lium, a GPU marketplace where independent providers list NVIDIA machines and renters pay by the second.

## What one hour costs (prices read 20 October 2026, 21:44 UTC)

Lium publishes its prices as a public feed, so these are the cheapest machines that were actually available to rent at the time of writing, not list prices:

| GPU | Memory per GPU | Lowest available price per GPU-hour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L40S | 48 GB | $0.38 |
| RTX A6000 | 48 GB | $0.42 |
| RTX 4090 | 24 GB | $0.55 (spot tier) |
| RTX 5090 | 32 GB | $0.90 |
| A100 80GB (8-GPU node) | 80 GB | $1.68 |
| H100 80GB (8-GPU node) | 80 GB | $1.80 (spot tier) |
| H200 (single GPU) | 141 GB | $3.50 |
| B200 | 180 GB | $5.00 |

Prices on a marketplace move with supply, so check the feed on the day you rent. At the time of writing the fleet had 1,835 GPUs listed, of which 229 were free to rent.

What that means for a fine-tune:

- A small LoRA run on a single 48 GB card (L40S or RTX A6000) costs under $0.50 for a full hour.
- A bigger model on one H200 with 141 GB of memory, enough to skip multi-GPU setup for many jobs, costs $3.50 for the hour.
- A full 8x H100 node for a heavier run costs $14.40 for the hour at the spot price above.

...

Lium bills per second at the hourly price, with no minimum. The formula in its billing docs is simply hourly price x seconds / 3600. A 10-minute smoke test on a $0.42 RTX A6000 costs about 7 cents. Charging stops at the moment you delete the pod, and a pod that fails to start is not charged.
